title: Toolchain choreography: streaming-aware result mediation and recursion sentinels
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a runtime-layer orchestration for multi-tool chaining that is natively streaming-aware, supports structured result injection into downstream tools, and enforces recursion/loop sentinels to prevent runaway invocations. This ticket covers the API contract, compatibility shim for older tool adapters, telemetry hooks for partial-result provenance, and a fallback path for degraded environments (e.g., non-streaming clients or restricted function-calling).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a 'choreographer' invocation contract that accepts a streaming input and a sequenced tool list and returns a stream of structured events (progress, tool_call, tool_result, finalization).
Tool result injection supports typed payloads with optional provenance headers so downstream tools can validate origin and schema before execution.

A recursion sentinel is implemented that detects repeated tool-call patterns within a request (configurable thresholds) and gracefully halts further tool invocation with a structured error and fallback suggestion.
Compatibility shim translates legacy synchronous tool adapters into the new streaming contract without requiring adapter rewrites.
End-to-end integration tests exercise multi-tool chains with streaming tokens, partial tool failures, and sentinel-triggered halts.
Documentation and public SDK examples (JS + Python) demonstrating structured result injection and how to opt into/override recursion thresholds.
technical_decisions: Use event-stream model (newline-delimited JSON) for inter-tool streaming events to keep wire format simple and compatible with current streaming endpoints.
Augment tool-result envelope with 'provenance' header (tool_id, invocation_id, partial=true|false, schema_version) so consumer tools can apply schema checks and caching keys.

Sentinel detection will be a sliding-window hash of (tool_id, normalized_input_signature) with decay and configurable limit per request; if threshold exceeded, issue a 'recursion_guard' event and stop further tool launches.
Implement compatibility shim at adapter layer: wrap legacy sync adapters in a small coroutine that emits a single tool_result event then closes stream; maintain same error mapping.
Telemetry: emit tracing spans with step-level latencies and an event tag for 'injected_result' vs 'generated_by_tool' to allow downstream cost attribution.
Default recursion threshold set to 6 repeats within a single request window; exposed as route-level config and per-request override via the API token's metadata.
implementation_notes: Add new choreographer API route: POST /v2/exec/choreograph with body: {streaming: true, chain: [{tool: "name", config: {...}}], input: stream}.
Create 'Event' enumeration: progress | call_request | call_result | injection | recursion_guard | complete | error.
Extend existing tool adapter interface with optional async iterator yield_event(event) so adapters can participate in streaming without breaking sync implementations.
Introduce a lightweight in-memory per-request sentinel cache keyed by (request_id) with bounded size; will later be backed by fast memcache for Dedicated scale.
Add unit-level schema definitions under/runtime/schemas for injection payloads and provenance headers; ensure backwards-compatible versioning.
Ensure that error paths always send a structured 'complete' event with non-zero code so clients can deterministically close streams.
rollout_plan: MVP: internal feature-flagged rollout to staging with compatibility shim enabled for all adapters (2 weeks).
Beta: invite 5 internal and 3 external partner teams to test multi-tool streaming chains and collect edge cases (3 weeks).
Gradual GA: enable on production for 10% traffic, monitor recursion guard rate and false positives, then 100% (2 weeks).
Post-GA: migrate sentinel cache from in-memory to memcached on Dedicated nodes and add dashboard in Console for recursion guard events.
test_plan: Unit tests for event marshaling/unmarshaling and provenance header enforcement.
Integration tests that run an instrumented chain of 4 tools with streaming token forwarding and verify order and partial-result visibility.
Chaos test: intermittent tool timeouts and partial failures; verify choreographer returns structured fallback and does not deadlock.
Sentinel stress test: synthetic loops to verify guard triggers within thresholds and that legitimate repeated calls (e.g., pagination) can be whitelisted.
monitoring_sla: Track recursion_guard events per 1000 requests, tool_call_latency P95, and stream_close_without_complete rate; alert on recursion_guard > 0.5% and stream_close_without_complete > 0.1%.
risks: False positives from sentinel heuristics may stop valid workflows (e.g., legitimate iterative refinement); mitigate with whitelisting and conservative defaults.
Adapters that perform side effects may not be safely replayable when retried; require an adapter capability flag 'idempotent' and fail closed otherwise.
Streaming clients behind proxies may buffer; need clear guidance and SDK helpers to surface partial events reliably.
Performance impact of per-request sentinel bookkeeping at very high QPS; plan to benchmark and lift to external cache early in Dedicated staging.
